page: Microsoft Azure D16ads_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on AMD EPYC 9V45 processors operating at up to 4.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 16 dedicated virtual CPUs derived from 8 physical cores via multithreading, paired with 64.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. For scratch storage and caching needs, the configuration bundles a 944 GB local NVMe SSD. It features hardware extensions including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16, but lacks dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark data reveals exceptional single-core processing capabilities alongside standard multi-core density. In stress-ng single-core tests, the server scored 3771.89, landing in the top 10% tier, mirrored by a Geekbench single-core score of 2773.0. Single-threaded gzip compression reached 41.68 GB/sec, and bzip3 decompression achieved 18.31 GB/sec, both placing within top-tier bands. Conversely, multi-threaded performance settles into the middle 50% across tests, including Geekbench multi-core at 15098.0 and stress-ng multi-core at 30095.88.

Memory bandwidth measurements register 50.99 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 34.16 GB/sec for writes. The machine performs solidly on integer-heavy processing, highlighted by Geekbench image processing in the top 25% and text processing at 3810.0 points in the top 10%. Small LLM inference runs quickly for CPU-bound tasks, with a 135M model generating 386.63 tokens/sec. However, LLM inference degrades noticeably under large model constraints, managing only 5.58 tokens/sec on 70B prompt processing without generating complete text output.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D16ads_v7 provides strong value for workloads requiring brisk single-thread throughput combined with bundled local NVMe storage. Tradeoffs center on average parallel scaling across its 16 vCPUs and the lack of discrete GPU compute. It is well-fitted for static web serving, enterprise application hosting, Redis caching layers, compilation pipelines, and transactional database instances leveraging low-latency local storage.
description: Microsoft Azure D16ads_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 16 dedicated vCPUs from an 8-core AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz, paired with 64.0 GB of memory and a bundled 944 GB local NVMe SSD. Operating without hardware acceleration, it delivers leading single-core performance, ranking in the top 10% on stress-ng and Geekbench single-thread benchmarks, as well as single-threaded compression tests. Multi-core performance aligns with the middle 50% average across PassMark and stress-ng metrics. The machine demonstrates solid capabilities in lightweight CPU-driven inference and image processing, while large model processing remains constrained by memory bandwidth. Balancing standard core density with rapid single-thread execution and high-speed local scratch disk, the D16ads_v7 serves as a robust platform for enterprise web applications, software compilation, caching, and mid-tier relational database environments.
